overview: This enum decides when an effect passes through destructible objects and traps.

None.simple: Destructible objects block the effect normally.
None.technical: This is the constructor default and the most common exported value. The contact switch falls through its default branch so a destructible object does not grant an early return. The effect contact handler keeps bThroughDestructible false, and the movement sweep runs for both destructible and trap components. A projectile effect with None also takes the early return in AGameTrap::ColParamSlot3 for ECC_GameTraceChannel8.

ThroughOnly.simple: The effect passes through destructible objects that have no defence.
ThroughOnly.technical: At destructible contact the switch returns early when Destructible.HasNoDefence is true. An intact destructible continues to the ground sound and contact path. In the movement sweep the destructible sweep still runs, and broken or non-destructible hits are not filtered here. Trap sweeps also still run.

Always.simple: The effect passes through destructible objects and traps in these paths.
Always.technical: The contact switch returns for any destructible object. The type-1 owner-contact handler sets bThroughDestructible because the byte is nonzero, and the destructible-owner check returns early. The movement sweep skips both the destructible-object sweep and the trap sweep.

AlwaysCheckObject.simple: The effect passes through broken objects while intact destructible objects still block it.
AlwaysCheckObject.technical: The contact switch returns for a destructible owner. The type-1 owner-contact handler treats this nonzero byte as through. In the movement sweep, hits are removed when the actor is not a destructible object or has break state 2 or 3, so only intact destructible objects remain to stop the move. The trap sweep still runs.

Invalid.simple: This value marks an invalid destructible-pass setting.
Invalid.technical: The enum declares it with value 255. No exported EffectDataTable row uses it and no named branch reads it, so its effect behavior is unknown.

notes: The effect row byte is read at row offset 0x47 and defaults to None.
The contact switch treats ThroughOnly by checking HasNoDefence. Always and AlwaysCheckObject both return early there.
In the movement sweep Always skips destructible and trap sweeps. AlwaysCheckObject removes broken and non-destructible hits before applying the blocking position.
The type-1 owner-contact handler uses a simpler nonzero test, so every declared non-None value sets bThroughDestructible in that path.
No exported EffectDataTable row uses Invalid.
